doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Travel with Art Blakey and passing on a California trip
summary: Southern-raised, he shrugged off travel conditions; he declined to cram in a car to California with Blakey's group.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you have any issues traveling with bands in — we’re talking let’s say the early 60s now, traveling around the country? What was that like?

It didn’t bother me because being born and raised in the south, in Richmond, Virginia, so you know you just get used to — you just let things go in one ear and right out the other. But I noticed back then though a lot of times you had to travel by car, that’s what my father and them did in the Harmonizing Four. And I think I messed up because when I was with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, I was supposed to — he was going to California and he did a — was going to do a recording, I think at Shelly Manne’s Hole or something. And the record was out and Chuck was one, but we all had to get in our car, it was six of us, and put the things on top. And I said I’m not going to California like that. But I shoulda went because they did a recording. But that’s the way it goes.

You know I had written a question down for later but I’ll ask it now because you said, “I’m not going to California like that.” And I wondered if over your career you have ever turned down a recording or a chance to play with some band for some personal reasons?
